Header:
Date: 2026-03-17
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~43 minutes
Attendees: Elena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Jasmine Khan (AtlasPay - Head of ML), Ravi Patel (AtlasPay - Platform), Laura Gomez (AtlasPay - Product)

Summary (auto):
Quick sync on the week 3 POC results: model selection narrowed to two variants (redwood-llama2-70b-q4 and redwood-mistral-7b-int8), discussion of pinning strategy, rollback/fallback options for Dedicated vs Hosted, and next steps to run validation and finalize canary plan. Action items captured.

Topics:
- Week 3 perf/cost review
- Model quality regressions on edge cases
- Version pinning strategy and rollbacks/fallbacks
- Network/VPC questions for Private test
- Next steps and schedule

Transcript:
00:00 Elena Park: All right hi everyone thanks for joining on a Tuesday afternoon, we'll keep this pretty tight, agenda two items: model selection follow-up and pinning/rollback strategy. Marcus is going to walk through the benchmarks.
00:18 Marcus Li: Hey, uh so I'll share my screen shortly, but quick recap: we ran the full 5k query set with the two candidate families, the redwood-llama2-70b-q4 which is our quantized 70b variant and the redwood-mistral-7b-int8 which is the smaller, faster footprint model. Average p95 latency on our hosted infra for llama2-70b-q4 was 420ms for 512 tokens, cost per 1k tokens estimated at $0.42. Mistral-7b-int8 was p95 140ms and cost about $0.12 per 1k.
00:45 Jasmine Khan: Sorry quick q, those numbers are on hosted or Dedicated? I thought we ran on Dedicated reserved pool last week.
00:52 Marcus Li: Good call, these were from the hosted benchmark run - we also have Dedicated numbers in the spreadsheet but there are some I/O things we need to normalize. Dedicated p95 for 70b was 360ms when pinned to the NVIDIA H100 pool, cost math differs due to commit.
01:10 Laura Gomez: From Product perspective latency is important but we care more about worst-case tail for chat interactions where user waits. Do we have failure rates?
01:20 Marcus Li: Yes failure rate (timeouts/retries) for llama2-70b-q4 was 0.8% in hosted runs and mistral-7b-int8 was 0.2%. We dug into the 0.8% and a chunk were OOMs on edge long-context cases, we traced those to a few specific prompt patterns that blow past the 2k token prefix cache assumptions.
01:39 Ravi Patel: That aligns with our internal tests - our customers sometimes feed in longer multi-turn history. We flagged that. Is there an auto fallback if the model OOMs?
01:47 Marcus Li: Right now our runtime will surface an OOM at the endpoint level; for POC you can configure a routing policy that on OOM falls back to a smaller compatible variant - e.g., route to mistral-7b-int8 if llama2 hits memory. We call it a model-fallback policy.
02:04 Jasmine Khan: Hmm can fallback impact semantics/consistency? If we fallback mid-conversation the style changes and product folks will complain.
02:12 Elena Park: Totally - that's why we recommend pinning a model version for a given route and exposing controlled fallbacks only for degraded cases, plus attributing in trace that fallback occurred. Also suggestion: have a rehydration step where you pass a short-system prompt to align tone if fallback happens.
02:32 Jasmine Khan: OK that helps. On quality the Mistral outputs scored slightly lower on our internal evals for summarization and legal-safety edge cases. We have some example failures in folder "atlaspay/poc/evals" - I'll share.
02:45 Marcus Li: We saw that too - Mistral-7b had few hallucination patterns on legal clauses, they were actually reproducible. Llama2-70b with q4 had better ROUGE/BLEU on your sets but cost and latency tradeoffs are material.
03:03 Laura Gomez: Could we do a hybrid routing? Like use the fast smaller model for intent/slot extraction and route to the big 70b for full summarization only when needed?
03:14 Marcus Li: Yes, the Redwood routing can do multi-model pipelines. You can do a classifier-first step on mistral then if confidence below X, forward to 70b. That reduces token spend. We can show a pattern doc.
03:28 Ravi Patel: For Private deployment - we need to know about KV cache sizes and whether the 70b will fit on our chosen node types. We are leaning towards on-prem H100s but need confirmation on quantized model memory footprint.
03:40 Marcus Li: The q4 quantized 70b will need ~90GB GPU memory for 2K context with typical KV structure; on H100 you've got headroom, but if you want two replicas and some margin I'd recommend 160GB total across the node. For int8 7b it's sub-20GB. I'll add specifics to the spreadsheet.
03:58 Jasmine Khan: Can you explain pinning vs version aliasing again? We were a bit fuzzy on the last call.
04:05 Elena Park: Sure - pinning locks the route to an explicit model version id, e.g., redwood-llama2-70b-q4-v3. Alias is a mutable pointer like "production-llama" that you can update. For POC we suggest pinning to a tested version for stable behavior, then use aliasing for gradual rollouts once you move to prod.
04:23 Jasmine Khan: And rollback strategy? If we update the alias and see regressions, is rollback instantaneous?
04:30 Marcus Li: Aliases can be re-pointed instantly; we also support automatic rollback policies where if a canary shows error rate > X or latency > Y it returns to previous. But note in Dedicated environments there can be warmup time if the prior model isn't resident. We have warmup preloading options.
04:52 Laura Gomez: What about observability - will we be able to see token-level cost and which requests used fallback?
04:58 Elena Park: Yes Console exposes per-request traces, token breakdowns, and tags for fallback/rollback events. We'll attach screenshots and the trace schema.
05:10 Jasmine Khan: On the POC deadline - we have internal stakeholder review on 2026-03-31. We need a recommended model to present. Ideally minimal regressions and acceptable cost.
05:23 Marcus Li: Given the evals and your quality constraints, our recommendation is to pin redwood-llama2-70b-q4 for the "summary" route and use redwood-mistral-7b-int8 for "fast-intent" route, with a fallback rule for long-context OOMs from 70b to Mistral.
05:40 Jasmine Khan: If we pin 70b, what's the expected incremental cost vs mistral for our 100k monthly tokens?
05:46 Marcus Li: Roughly $0.42 vs $0.12 per 1k, so monthly delta for 100k tokens ~ $30. You should validate on your exact token distribution; I've put cost sims in the sheet.
06:02 Ravi Patel: Network question: for Private test we'll need VPC peering and SAML SSO for the control plane - can you share docs and do we need static IPs?
06:12 Elena Park: Yes we'll send the Private onboarding doc; static IPs are optional but helpful for firewall rules. We support SAML SSO and KMS integrations. I'll follow up.
06:25 Jasmine Khan: We also want to capture sample regression cases to show to legal if needed. Marcus can you flag top 50 failure prompts?
06:33 Marcus Li: Yep will export top 50 with diffs and example token traces.
06:38 Laura Gomez: And for rollout, can we do a canary that sends 5% traffic to new alias while 95% stays pinned?
06:44 Marcus Li: Absolutely, routing policies support weight-based canaries plus auto rollback triggers. We can demo that in the canary walkthrough.
06:52 Elena Park: Ok let's recap next steps quickly. Marcus will share updated benchmark CSV with Dedicated/Hosted normalized numbers and memory footprints. Jasmine will run the 2k validation test against the recommended pinned Llama model and share regressions. Ravi will send VPC topology questions. Redwood will schedule a canary demo.
07:12 Jasmine Khan: One more Q on security: do you keep audit logs for private plane operations and can we integrate with our SIEM?
07:20 Elena Park: Yes audit logs available, long retention is an add-on but we support log forwarding to your SIEM; Marcus will include specifics.
07:28 Ravi Patel: Cool thanks.
07:31 Elena Park: All right thanks everyone, we'll follow up with artifacts and action items; meeting adjourned.

Notes: Transcript has occasional transcription errors (model names sometimes 'Lama' or 'Mistral seven') and speaker overlaps. References: spreadsheet "atlaspay/poc/benchmarks-2026-03-17.csv", evals folder "atlaspay/poc/evals" and canary playbook link will be shared in follow up.
